content.title: Former Fed governor's stock trades violated the central bank's ethics rules
content.summary: A former Federal Reserve governor who retired in August listed several stock trades in her financial disclosure documents for 2024 that violated the central bank's ethics rules.  The transactions are outlined in a report released Saturday by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics, which reviewed Adriana Kugler's financial disclosures after the Fed referred them to its inspector general earlier this year.  Kugler, who unexpectedly stepped down from the Fed board Aug. 8, disclosed more than a dozen individual stock trades, including several made during financial trading “blackout periods” around the time the Federal Reserve's policymaking committee meets to set interest rates and other monetary policy.

thumbnail.caption: FILE - Adriana Kugler speaks during a Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee hearing to examine her nomination to be a member of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, June 21, 2023, on Capitol Hill in Washington. (AP Photo/Mariam Zuhaib, File)

content.title: Airlines will need time to 'smooth out' following gov't shutdown
content.description:
While President Trump signed a federal funding bill that reopened the US government earlier this week, does this give enough time for the airline industry to bounce back and get its ducks in a row before Americans take to the skies for Thanksgiving?

The Points Guy Director of Content Eric Rosen sits down with Myles Udland on Market Domination Overtime to talk about recent flight cancellations and the advantages of TSA PreCheck ahead of the busy holiday travel season.

At Yahoo Finance Invest, Delta Air Lines (DAL) CEO Ed Bastian called the government shutdown "inexcusable" and "incredibly disruptive."

Also hear Bloomberg Intelligence senior analyst George Ferguson's thoughts on holiday travel disruptions.

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Domination Overtime.
